subject: flamingo
pitch: An elegant flamingo standing tall in shallow water. Candy-pink feathers deepening to coral on the wings, with a flash of black flight feathers at the wing tips, an S-curved neck, a bent beak that is pale pink with a black tip, pale yellow eyes and long rose-coloured legs with knobbly knees and webbed feet.
reasoning:
I'm planning a compact flamingo model standing on two legs in shallow water, using a flat translucent-looking disc for the water surface with legs sinking slightly below it.

For the skeleton, I'm working out joint positions for the body ellipsoid and the leg chains—hip, knee, ankle, and foot joints with realistic flamingo proportions where the visible long segment is actually the tarsus bending backward at the "knee."

Now I'm sketching the neck as an S-curve made of several catmull points rising from the body front up to the head, aiming for an overall height around 1.5-1.6 units which is a bit tall for a real flamingo but acceptable for this model.

I'm setting up the neck chain with tapering radius from a thicker base to a slimmer top near the head, then placing a head joint at the chain tip with a small sphere for the skull, followed by a downward-bent upper beak.

Now I'm shaping the upper mandible as a sweep path curving from the face forward and down, tapering the radius and coloring it pale pink transitioning to black near the tip. I'm also adding a separate lower jaw bone with its own thinner tapered path and matching black tip, defining the beak cross-section as a flattening ellipse for a more realistic shape.

For the eyes I'm placing small pale yellow spheres with tiny black pupils on either side of the head. For the body I'm using a scaled sphere for the torso plus another for the chest, flattened wedge shapes for tail feathers, and I'm weighing whether to keep the wings folded against the body or extended, settling on a folded resting pose with jointed wings for flexibility.

Now I'm building each wing as a shoulder-elbow-wrist chain with coral coverts made from scaled spheres, fanned cone shapes for the tertial feathers at the back, and an extruded black flight-feather block near the rear of the wing.

Still building wing geometry...

Setting wing chain names for shoulder, elbow, wrist on each side, parented to root, with bones assigned for black wingtips and the elbow plate. For colors I'm going pink-to-coral: candy pink body, lighter pink neck, coral wings, with a subtle mottled variation on the body paint, and rose-colored knobbly legs.

Now I'm building the feet: knee and ankle joints as small spheres, three forward-webbed toes as thin rods, plus a short hind toe, with a flat triangular web slab connecting the toe tips using Newell's method for consistent normals.

I'm tuning the water level so it sits around 0.02 high while the feet rest at 0.03, keeping the toe rods and webbing partially visible above the surface rather than fully submerged, with ripple rings planned next.

Now I'm working out the skeleton rig: a root joint at the hips, a spine joint for the body, and a tail chain running from the rump back and down through two segments, with the tail feathers swept as a flattened, tapering shape.

Plotting the neck curve points to form an S-shape, with the head tilting forward at the top, and tapering the neck radius gradually with a slight bulge partway up.

Now I'm setting up the head joints: a jaw joint and a head sphere colored pale pink, then building the beak as two curved paths—upper and lower—starting from inside the head and bending downward to form the pointed shape.

I'm tapering the beak with radius functions so it narrows toward the tip, giving the upper mandible a rounded cap and adding a black band near the end to match flamingo coloring, with the base staying paler and slightly wider. Now I'm thinking about adding a few coral tertial feather spikes drooping from the rump to suggest wing plumage.

Setting up the builder with a root joint, then defining the leg structure with hip, knee, and ankle points -- I'm working out the forward/backward z-offsets so the ankle bends correctly for that distinctive flamingo leg shape.

Building the leg geometry: sweeping a polyline through the hip, knee, ankle, and foot with a tapering radius array, then adding small spheres at the joints to give a knobbly knee-and-ankle look.

Now I'm adding the three forward toes plus a hind toe off the foot, each as a tapering rod, and connecting their tips with a thin webbed polygon slab for the foot.

I'm adding ripple rings around each foot using thin flattened torus shapes, plus a wide shallow cylinder for the water surface beneath them.
